planCommit: xqtqnrsy fdb7e7fb docs(plans): LEGION-29 heartbeat role re-assertion plan
summary: Session-side only: envoy.ts's heartbeat tick, after a successful registerSession(), runs reassertRole — GET /v1/roles/<role>; a soft POST /v1/roles/set only when the listener does not name this session; 409 drops the local claim, warns once (ui.notify), ends re-assertion; no appendEntry on regain or on 409; a regain fires onEnvoyRoleRegained(role, reason) on the existing LEGION_ROLE_CLAIM_BRIDGE symbol. legion.ts registers the hook: controller → controllerReady({secret, sessionId}) again; root architect → processReady again (with its generation); phase worker → nothing. No listener or daemon change. One PR on legion/LEGION-29.

refinementsToSpec.text: The regain hook also fires on the first healthy heartbeat after a registry outage (reason "reregistered") even when the claim survived. Reason: after a listener outage longer than the envoy_sessions TTL the durable claim is intact but liveRoleHolder answers no-holder until the session re-registers; the daemon's controller-kind publishes in that window land in controllerPendingNotices and only /controller/ready drains them (index.ts:625-628). The spec's GET-based detection cannot see that hole because the re-registration itself restores the holder before the GET runs. Acceptance 6's 'controllerPendingNotices: 0 after the drain' needs this. Cost: one idempotent ready call per observed outage. Architect vetoes before Task 2 or it stands.

A 409 writes no transcript entry (mirrors setEnvoyRole's refused soft reclaim, envoy.ts:390-398): the drop is claimedRoleTopic = undefined only, so a later omp --resume still lets the listener arbitrate from the transcript.
When GET names a different holder the heartbeat still issues the soft claim and lets the listener's atomic rule answer (409, or success if that holder died in between). One arbiter, one code path.

forensics.verdict: (b) — a variant through the deployed image's code: at the deployed commit fcd13a14 the interest reaper Reap() (StartReaper 5 min / 10 min grace, cmd/listener/main.go) calls Remove(sid, nil) → releaseAllRoleClaims(sid) for every session whose envoy_sessions Get fails (any KV error counts as dead) and whose interest row UpdatedAt is >10 min stale (upserts failed for minutes before each self-termination). 37 sessions were reaped 05:23–07:17Z with the listener up. Not (a): envoy_roles is 5 months older than the image. (c) unsupported: only transient client timeouts; post-restart reaper cycles reaped 0; role deliveries continued. The literal ReleaseExpiredRoleClaim (PR #958, merged 2026-09-12T07:09:41Z) is not in the deployed binary.

daemonFindings.controller: HTTP 404 → publishOrThrow pushes controllerPendingNotices (events.ts:470-489) → onUndeliverable (index.ts:517-531) → ensureController (processes.ts:1396-1418) is a no-op for a live controller whose daemon-side claim is still set. Only /controller/ready drains (api/routes/controller.ts:11-28 → index.ts:625-628). Regain must re-run controller/ready; repeat-safe (same path /legion-claim-controller re-runs).
daemonFindings.rootArchitect: onUndeliverable → resumeWorker(root, tree, 'architect') (index.ts:523-527); the root claim {issue, role, sessionId, agentId} (api/routes/process.ts:47-52) has no locator/resumeSessionFile → resumeWorker no-op guard (processes.ts:1841-1846). Only the exceptions lane (handleException processes.ts:1795-1820 → reclaim-architect controlDirective 1707-1734) redelivers, and it never fires for the daemon's own HTTP 404. Regain must re-run /process/ready: handleProcessReady (api/routes/process.ts:71-96) 409s only on generation mismatch, confirmRootReady (processes.ts:1503-1509) has no already-confirmed guard, onTreeReady → emitOverseerCatchup (index.ts:509-515, wired at 616) republishes the state-derived catch-up, markTreeReady reuses the cached client (2242-2244).
daemonFindings.phaseWorker: onUndeliverable → resumeWorker → workerCatchup → spawnWorker (processes.ts:1847-1849); with locator/sessionId/readyConfirmedAt set it probes the socket (539-543) and resumeOrQueueExisting (565-574) prompts an idle worker below the cap or queues for the next idle. /worker/ready on a confirmed claim is a no-op (workerReady 692-743, 720-723; handleWorkerReady api/routes/workers.ts:273-294). Nothing to re-run; the plan pins the no-op in a test.
